title: Region health: add cache TTL + jitter to avoid stampedes during partial outages
author: Miles Thornton
release_notes: Region health service now caches read results with jittered TTL to reduce downstream load and prevent thundering herd when signal backends are degraded; adds metrics for cache hit ratio and stale-read rate.
body: Summary: This PR introduces a small but important performance + resiliency tweak to the Region Health Service (added in PR-19810) by caching health read results with a configurable TTL and per-key jitter. During partial outages (e.g., probe stream delays, metrics backend slowness, or control plane read spikes), callers were re-evaluating region health too frequently and in lock-step, causing request stampedes against upstream inputs and amplifying the impairment. Motivation/Context: In staging rehearsals for the Regional Failover Automation Upgrade, we saw synchronized bursts of /v1/region-health reads from routing/policy evaluation when one of the input streams slowed down; the service would continuously re-fetch and re-aggregate with minimal reuse. This increases tail latency and can create self-inflicted pressure right when we need stable signal evaluation. Approach: 1) Add an in-memory cache around the aggregated RegionHealth snapshot keyed by (environment, region, service_tier) with TTL and jitter; 2) Use a "stale-if-error" behavior: if refreshing from upstream fails or times out, return the last known snapshot for a bounded grace period (with an explicit freshness field) to keep routing evaluation deterministic while not hammering upstreams; 3) Add metrics + logs so on-call can distinguish cache protection from true upstream recovery. The jitter is applied as: effective_ttl = base_ttl * (1 + rand(-jitter_pct, +jitter_pct)) to desynchronize refresh boundaries across replicas and keys. Defaults: base_ttl=5s, jitter_pct=0.2, stale_grace=30s. These are intentionally conservative to avoid hiding real region events; ADR-042 still treats reachability and error-burn as authoritative, and this change is about how often we recompute the same aggregation. Configuration: Adds config knobs to region-health-service: REGION_HEALTH_CACHE_TTL, REGION_HEALTH_CACHE_JITTER_PCT, REGION_HEALTH_CACHE_STALE_GRACE_TTL. The service emits the following new metrics: region_health_cache_hits_total, region_health_cache_misses_total, region_health_cache_stale_serves_total, region_health_refresh_failures_total, and a gauge region_health_snapshot_age_seconds. Changed areas (high-level): - services/region-health/cache.ts: TTL cache with jitter + stale-if-error wrapper - services/region-health/aggregate.ts: plumbs freshness/age through the snapshot model - services/region-health/http/handlers.ts: response includes snapshot_age_seconds and snapshot_freshness={fresh|stale} in headers for debugging (internal only) - observability/metrics/region_health.yaml: adds metrics definitions and dashboards hook points - tests: unit tests for jitter bounds, expiry, stale-if-error, and refresh timeout behavior Test Plan: - Unit: region-health cache jitter range and expiration; stale serve when refresh fails; age monotonicity - Integration (staging): replay recorded slow-probe stream; verify cache hit ratio increases and upstream query rate decreases; verify routing evaluation remains stable - Load: synthetic 500 RPS region-health reads with upstream latency injected; verify p99 improves and upstream call QPS drops Checklist: - [x] Added metrics and log fields (cache_status, snapshot_age_seconds) - [x] Verified no new high-cardinality labels (no tenant_id dimension) - [x] Confirmed default TTL doesn’t exceed failover trigger evaluation cadence assumptions - [x] Updated runbook notes (internal link in code comment) Related: ENG-2413 (Region Health Service), ENG-2412 (signal hierarchy). This is intended to be a safe prerequisite for game day readiness and complements PR-19812 (deterministic signal priority) by reducing recomputation churn under degraded conditions.
commits: region-health: add ttl cache wrapper with jitter
region-health: stale-if-error bounded grace and snapshot age
metrics: add cache hit/miss + refresh failure counters
tests: cover expiry/jitter bounds and stale behavior
chore: wire config defaults + docs comments
review_conversation: Ravi Menon: Can we confirm TTL won’t delay detection for reachability-based triggers? I don’t want the cache to hold onto a bad state for too long during a real regional partition.

Miles Thornton (author): Yes—reachability probes are still ingested on their own cadence, and the cache TTL only affects how often we recompute the aggregation. Also, we return snapshot_age_seconds; policy engine can require freshness for certain trigger types if needed. Defaults are 5s TTL + 30s stale grace only on refresh failures, not on normal operation.
Allison Grant: Please avoid adding snapshot_freshness as a metric label; keep it as a field/log or separate counters. Otherwise we risk label growth once we add more freshness states.
Miles Thornton (author): Agreed. Implemented separate counters (stale_serves_total) instead of a label, and snapshot_freshness is only in structured logs + an internal response header.
Victor Alvarez: What happens if upstream timeouts correlate across replicas? Jitter helps, but do we also have singleflight to dedupe refreshes per key within a process?
Miles Thornton (author): Added per-key in-process singleflight so concurrent callers await one refresh; jitter desynchronizes across processes/replicas. Documented in cache.ts.
Ethan Park: +1. One nit: make REGION_HEALTH_CACHE_JITTER_PCT clamp to [0, 1] and reject negatives.
Miles Thornton (author): Done; added validation + tests.
Ravi Menon: LGTM after validation change.
